SW 2025 rev 33.1.1 live test LiveSimulationStaticTests.test_apply_force_load_converts_units_and_reads_the_magnitude_back: on the 600 mm IPE beam, AddForce2(swsForceTypeNormal=1, swsSelectionFaceEdgeVertexPoint=0, entities, Nothing, err) created the load, ForceBeginEdit + NormalForceOrTorqueValue + ForceEndEdit returned 0, ICWLoadsAndRestraintsManager.Count grew and ICWForce.ForceType read back 1. The tool takes magnitude plus an optional unit (default N): 2 kN was stored and read back as exactly 2000.0 N, and 200 kg as exactly 200 * 9.80665 = 1961.33 N, so kg and t are masses converted with g = 9.80665 m/s2 while N, kN and kgf are forces. A separate probe confirmed the set/read-back is exact for 1.0, 2.5, 1000.0 and 5000.0 N.

Blocked alternative: AddForce3 (the 20-argument overload) raises DISP_E_ARRAYISLOCKED ('Memory is locked') for every Comps marshalling tried (Python list, SAFEARRAY of R8, SAFEARRAY of VARIANT), so a force with X/Y/Z components or a moment pair is not offered yet.

Torque is offered instead: apply_force_load(load_type='torque', reference=<reference axis feature>) uses swsForceTypeTorque (2) with the axis feature as RefGeom. The add-in accepts the IFeature itself or a cylindrical face there, and returns error 4 (swsForceErrorSelectReferenceAxisOrCylindricalFace) for anything else; passing the axis's IRefAxis instead raises DISP_E_ARRAYISLOCKED. SW 2025 rev 33.1.1 live test LiveSimulationStaticTests.test_pressure_load_matches_the_equivalent_force: on the 600 mm DIN IPE beam, 0.02 MPa on the 132000 mm2 flange was created with AddPressure(swsPressureTypeNormal=0, DispArray, Nothing, err) (LoadsAndRestraintsManager.Count 1 to 2, PressureType 0), and the physical cross-check passed: applying the equivalent 2640 N as one normal force in a second study deflected the beam by the same maximum displacement within 5 percent, so the stored pascal value cannot be off by a unit factor.

Empirical, from the installed cosworks.tlb and a live probe: the add-in ignores writes to ICWPressure.Unit inside PressureBeginEdit (the property still read 0 = Pascal afterwards), so a value of 0.02 would have meant 0.02 Pa, not 0.02 MPa. The tool therefore reads the unit the load reports, converts the requested pressure into that unit (swsStrengthUnit_e to pascal), stores it and verifies the read-back; an unsupported unit index fails with PRESSURE_UNIT_UNSUPPORTED. Accepted input units: Pa, kPa, MPa, N/mm2, bar, kgf/cm2, psi, ksi.

requested_behavior: Fast and detailed traversal modes for large assemblies
evidence: list_components now takes mode='fast'|'detailed' (default detailed, so existing callers and their transforms/suppression keep working) and inspect_document exposes the same choice as component_mode. Fast mode reads only Name2 and GetPathName per instance and descends solely into components whose referenced document ends with .SLDASM; a known .SLDPRT instance is a leaf and receives no further calls at all. An unresolved or empty path counts as unknown and is still descended into, so a virtual sub-assembly cannot be missed.

Measured live 24 September 2026 on the GrabCAD assembly 'Stopnice v prostoru - Z ograjo' (77 instances: 11 top-level, 66 nested up to level 3), same session: list_components(depth=1, fast) 0.17 s / 11 instances; list_components(depth=32, fast) 36.20 s / 77 instances; list_components(depth=32, detailed) 137.05 s / 77 instances, so the full tree is 3.8x faster and the fast tree still contains every instance with complete coverage. inspect_document(sections=summary,assembly,dependencies, depth=32, component_mode='fast') took 51.14 s for the same 77 instances. The remaining cost is the two unavoidable member reads per nested instance plus GetChildren on the sub-assemblies, not the data itself.

Live test LiveComponentModeTests.test_fast_and_detailed_find_the_same_profile_instances builds a saved assembly from real DIN IPE weldment members (a 600 mm beam plus a sub-assembly holding two 300 mm beams) and asserts that fast and detailed report the same instance paths and a complete coverage, that the sub-assembly is recognised from its .sldasm path with both nested leaves found, that fast items carry no transform, configuration or suppression_state, and that detailed mode still returns a 16-element transform and a suppression state for every instance.

10 focused unit tests in solidworks_mcp/tests/test_component_traversal_modes.py count the COM member accesses on fakes and prove a leaf part is asked only for Name2 and GetPathName in fast mode while detailed mode reads all eight members.
